_about: The line an agent reads for an event defined without text (TypeScript text, Python text=, Go Text): the event's description with its whitespace collapsed to single spaces and trailing periods and whitespace trimmed, then, if any argument is left, " (" + the arguments joined by ", " + ")". Each argument is "<key> <value>": keys in name order; an argument whose value is null (or absent) or the empty string is skipped; a string is written raw (not quoted, not trimmed); any other value is compact JSON as JavaScript's JSON.stringify writes it (no spaces, non-ASCII and <, >, & unescaped, a number with no fraction written without one). No arguments left: the description alone, with no parentheses. Only top-level null and empty-string values are skipped: inside an array or object they stay. Nested objects here list their keys in name order, so the case doesn't depend on how an SDK orders a nested object's keys. Each SDK's tests render every case with the event's default text (TypeScript WakeEvent.render, Python _default_text, Go defaultText) from description and args, and compare it with want exactly. Loaders drop top-level keys that start with _.
